classification.difficultyReason: Infer that the recombined triangles have base b−a, express both component areas symbolically, and simplify their sum to the trapezium formula. The supplied decomposition and addition scaffold guide the derivation.

content.prompt: Using the diagram and your knowledge of the area of composite figures, derive the area of a trapezium by splitting a trapezium up into a rectangle and triangles.

spec.description: Horizontal trapezium split by two vertical segments into a central rectangle and two side triangles. Capped dimensions label the top side a, bottom side b and perpendicular height h. Both parallel markers point left.
spec.mathematics: The rectangle has width a and height h. The two triangular bases together have length b-a. Drawing coordinates reproduce the visible proportions and are not additional numerical givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, region distinctions and a, b, h dimension labels remain visible in the student question; no area expressions are supplied.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, detached rectangle in the middle.
spec.description: Upright rectangle matching the central rectangular region of the original trapezium.
spec.mathematics: Its width and height correspond to a and h in the original figure. The common vertical coordinate frame preserves the original figures' relative scale and baseline.
spec.answerVisibility: The detached region is visible; its area is an editable response directly below.

answer.worked:
The rectangle has width $a$ and height $h$.
$$A_1=ah$$

spec.sourceRegion: Question 10, recombined triangles to the right of the detached rectangle.
spec.description: One upright triangle with a horizontal base and a vertical internal dividing segment from the apex to a point left of the base midpoint.
spec.mathematics: The two original side triangles are recombined with total base b-a and height h. Their unequal bases and the asymmetric divider are retained. No new numerical measurements are stated.
spec.answerVisibility: The recombined figure remains visible; its area is an editable response directly below.

answer.worked:
The combined triangle has base $b-a$ and height $h$.
$$A_2=\frac{h}{2}(b-a)$$

answer.short: $A=\frac{h}{2}(a+b)$. Add the rectangle area $ah$ and the combined triangle area $\frac{h}{2}(b-a)$.
